title.narrative: The Borno Lean Season OneStop Resilience Network Programme – Pilot in Monguno LGA

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtGOALPrime Organization Nigeria (GPON), in consortium with Solidarités International (SI) and Novel Alliance for Development Aid (NADA), proposes a six-month integrated Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) and Child Protection (CP) emergency response project in Monguno LGA, Borno State.lt/pgtltpgt lt/pgtltpgtThe project targets 25,450 conflict-affected individuals—20,850 through WASH services and 4,600 through CP interventions. with a demographic breakdown of 60% IDPs and 40% host community members, and 15% persons with disabilities (PwDs. Women and girls will make up 60% of the total beneficiaries. This project is designed to directly complement the ECHO-funded WASH project jointly implemented by GPON and SI in Monguno.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtThe WASH component will be implemented by GPON with technical support from SI, while the Child Protection component will be implemented by NADA with technical support from GPON.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtThe WASH response will focus on complimenting the effort of the ongoing ECHO funded WASH project ensuring a minimum water supply- (through direct reticulation of free flow boreholes without pumping, networking of silo operated water supplies, routine operation maintenance including repairs of leaks and bursts, replacement of fast wearing or damaged fittings, chlorination and chlorine monitoring), and the reform of WASH management committees. In sanitation, activities will include latrine desludging, minor repairs, allocation of latrines to HHs to operate, construction of additional latrines for marginalized households, and PwDs. lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtThe Child Protection response aims to strengthen community-based protection structures to prevent and respond to child protection concerns at both camp and host community levels, in coordination with partners delivering other support services. Core activities will include: Case management for vulnerable children at risk, family tracing and reunification of unaccompanied and separated children, including those formerly associated with armed groups, community-based reintegration support for children associated with armed groups, community awareness, psychosocial, and recreational activities to promote emotional well-being and resilience, positive parenting sessions and life skills education for adolescents and caregivers, strengthening community-based reporting systems for abuse, neglect, and exploitation through established channels and targeted awareness-raising.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtThe consortium seeks to pioneer a localization initiative that delivers a holistic capacity-building and knowledge transfer process to local partners. As the only INGO in the consortium, SI brings strategic value through a structured capacity-building and oversight package, targeting both GPON and NADA. Drawing on lessons learned from prior NHF projects and pooled fund initiatives in Northeast Nigeria, SI will provide a tailored package of institutional support including: lt/pgtltpgt(i) Development of internal control systems and compliance tools, lt/pgtltpgt(ii) Risk mitigation measures and spot checks, lt/pgtltpgt(iii) Harmonization of procurement and HR processes, and lt/pgtltpgt(iv) Peer learning sessions and mentorship on donor compliance and grants management. lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis model directly supports the NHF’s localization agenda by addressing root causes of risk classification, reducing dependency on international actors, and increasing the operational maturity of national NGOs. Through joint technical missions, training modules, and documentation support, the project aims to improve the risk rating of GPON from high to low, while ensuring accountable and high-quality service delivery to vulnerable populations in Monguno ltbrgtlt/pgt
